name: Tetrodotoxin Gland Implantation
description: Introduces pufferfish toxin-producing bacterial symbionts into modified sweat glands in the palms, creating a contact-delivery venom system. When activated voluntarily through a stress-hormone trigger, the palms secrete a thin film of tetrodotoxin — enough to cause numbness, paralysis, and potentially death through skin contact. The activation requires deliberate effort; accidental poisoning is rare but not impossible. The user is immune to their own toxin through co-expressed sodium channel modifications. Gravemoss Biofoundry's version includes a visible warning coloration — the palms flush bright orange when toxin is active, an aposematic signal borrowed from poison dart frogs. Black-market versions skip the warning coloration, creating invisible poisoners. The modification is the most legally restricted geneware in Meridian 88 after military-grade installations.
source_organism: Takifugu rubripes (Japanese pufferfish), Vibrio alginolyticus (TTX-producing bacteria)
legality: Restricted (requires defensive permit; unregistered installation is a felony-equivalent offense)
procedure: Palmar gland implantation surgery with bacterial symbiont introduction, 2 sessions
expression_time: 4–6 weeks for gland maturation; toxin production reaches full potency at 3 months
reversibility: Glands can be surgically removed; bacterial colonies must be eliminated with targeted antibiotics over 6 weeks
side_effects: Palms tingle constantly when toxin reserves are full
Accidental activation during extreme stress or nightmares
Intimate contact requires conscious suppression — relationships are complicated
Toxin potency fluctuates with diet and health
social_perception: Feared and stigmatized. Registered TTX users must disclose their modification in many contexts. Unregistered users face severe legal consequences. Some view it as a necessary self-defense tool; others see it as the mark of someone prepared to kill with a handshake.
story_hooks: A TTX user is accused of a contact-poison murder, but their toxin profile doesn't match the one found on the victim — someone is synthesizing a copycat toxin to frame them
A black-market TTX installation goes wrong, producing toxin continuously without voluntary control — the user can't touch anyone without poisoning them
